title: AngularJS 1.8 is past its end of life (2021-12-31)
technical_impact: Release cycle 1.8 of angularjs gets no security or bug fixes since 2021-12-31. The newest cycle is 1.8.
business_impact: Part of the system runs on AngularJS 1.8, which its maker stopped fixing on 2021-12-31. New security holes will stay open, and auditors and insurers usually flag this.
recommendation: Plan an upgrade of AngularJS to a supported release (1.8 or another supported cycle).

title: angular 1.8 has 10 known vulnerabilities
technical_impact: OSV lists GHSA-2qqx-w9hr-q5gx, GHSA-2vrf-hf26-jrp5, GHSA-4w4v-5hc9-xrr2, GHSA-7x27-g8rg-x87w, GHSA-j58c-ww9w-pwp5, GHSA-m2h2-264f-f486… for this exact version. angular vulnerable to regular expression denial of service via the $resource service; angular vulnerable to regular expression denial of service via the angular.copy() utility
business_impact: angular 1.8, a library the system depends on, has publicly known security flaws. Attackers read these lists too.
recommendation: Upgrade angular to a version without these advisories and re-test the features that use it.

title: 5 complex files change far more often than the rest
technical_impact: These files combine high branching with frequent edits: the places where defects and merge conflicts concentrate.
business_impact: A small set of files absorbs most of the changes and most of the risk. Every new feature that touches them costs more and breaks more often.
recommendation: Cover these files with tests first, then split them along their responsibilities before any larger migration.

title: No changes since 2020-06-05
technical_impact: The last commit is more than two years old; the build tools and dependencies have likely drifted.
business_impact: Nobody has changed this system in years. Even small fixes will first need someone to make it build and run again.
recommendation: Before planning changes, prove the system still builds and runs in a clean environment.

title: No container or infrastructure-as-code definitions
technical_impact: The runtime environment is not described in code, so it cannot be recreated automatically.
business_impact: Setting up a new server or a test environment is manual work that only a few people know how to do.
recommendation: Describe the runtime in a Dockerfile or IaC as a first, low-risk modernization step.

title: No logging or monitoring library detected
technical_impact: No known logging, tracing or metrics library is declared in the manifests or configuration.
business_impact: When something fails in production it is hard to know what happened or how often.
recommendation: Add structured logging and basic health metrics before any migration, to compare before and after.
